newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen testing 113.00 yen support in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen testing 113.00 yen support in Asia.

text.p: The dollar may test below a key technical support of 113.00 yen in Asia on Friday after falling moderately overnight, traders said.
Bids are expected by Japanese institutional investors, including life insurers, below 113 yen, while offers are also thought to be lined up above 113.50 yen, they said.

"We want to see whether the dollar will be firmly supported at 113.00 yen," a trader at a Japanese trust bank said. "If the dollar fails to break that level, then short-holders will be covering their positions. But a decisive break below that level could send the dollar to as low as 112.70."
Traders said speculative sales dragged down the dollar to near 113.00 yen in New York as buying of the yen intensified amid growing credit-tightening speculation.

They said market participants would closely watch the release of Japan's preliminary industrial output data for May and forecasts for June and July at 0430 GMT to judge the trend for Japanese interest rates.

"The market is focusing more into the fate of Japanese interest rates, particularly since the tankan data (released on Wednesday) was stronger than expectations and pushed up Japanese interest rates," a trader at a commercial bank said.
Traders are also focusing on a speech by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita to be given at 0340 GMT.
"We want to hear what Governor Matsushita says about the Japanese economy," the commercial bank trader said.
The dollar was capped against the yen overnight by the Japanese currency's strength against the mark. The yen rose nearly a full yen against the mark to 65.55 in New York.

Traders said Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen triggered modest mark sales in European trading when he told an audience in Frankfurt he could not rule out a cut in interest rates, even though he did not see one on the horizon.
Traders said the greenback is likely to be weighted above 1.7300 marks in Asia and supported at 1.7200 marks.
In early Asian trade, the dollar stood little changed from New York levels at around 113.10/20 yen.
Traders said some stop-loss selling orders could be triggered should the dollar break below 112.80-90 yen.
